findings.claim: If sequences must instead be replayed from a buffer starting mid-episode (offline distillation), stored-hidden-state + burn-in is the standard fix for recurrent state staleness: R2D2 stores length-80 sequences overlapping by 40, never crossing episode boundaries, with a stored initial hidden state and a burn-in prefix used only to warm the LSTM before loss is applied.
findings.source: Kapturowski et al., 'Recurrent Experience Replay in Distributed RL' (R2D2), ICLR 2019, openreview r1lyTjAqYX
findings.relevance: Only needed if the fallback is built as offline BC over logged sequences. The on-policy kickstart pattern avoids the whole issue — one more reason to prefer it given the LSTM(128) student.

findings.claim: Value function: Kickstarting does NOT use the teacher's critic — the student's value head trains on environment rewards concurrently because RL and distillation run jointly from step one, so when lambda decays the critic is already calibrated. Czarnecki adds that a teacher's critic, if available, is mainly useful to correct IMPERFECT teachers (their 'teacher V reward' variant: r_hat = r + V_teacher(s') - V_student(s)). QDagger (Reincarnating RL) likewise runs distillation + TD loss jointly and decays the distillation coefficient over training ('weaning').
findings.source: Schmitt et al. arXiv:1803.03835 Eq. 3 (read from PDF); Czarnecki et al. AISTATS 2019 Sec 4/Table 1 (read from PDF); Agarwal et al., 'Reincarnating RL', NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2206.01626
findings.relevance: Answer to sub-question 4: the student does NOT need the teachers' value functions IF distill and PPO run jointly — the critic self-trains on returns during distillation. What it does need is for the value head to be trained before the distill loss is fully weaned. Avoid a pure supervised phase followed by cold-start PPO.

findings.claim: If a pure supervised distill phase is used anyway, the documented failure is the fresh random critic: right after cloning, advantage estimates are noise and early PPO updates can collapse the cloned policy. Documented mitigations: (a) freeze the policy head and run critic-only updates until value loss stabilizes before unfreezing (used in recent BC+PPO pipelines, e.g. SABR 2025 and residual-RL finetuning papers); (b) AlphaStar's approach — keep a KL penalty to the supervised/cloned policy during all subsequent RL, which both preserves the cloned skills and aids exploration.
findings.source: SABR, arXiv:2509.10486 and Residual Off-Policy RL for Finetuning BC Policies, arXiv:2509.19301 (critic warmup); Vinyals et al., AlphaStar, Nature 2019 (KL to supervised policy during RL) via The Gradient analysis cyk1337.github.io
findings.relevance: The 'optional low-LR RL polish' in the fallback plan needs one of these two guards. The cheapest robust combo for this codebase: 20-30M steps of critic-only warmup at the end of distillation (policy frozen), then polish with a small KL-to-distilled-policy anchor.

findings.claim: Typical student:teacher ratios — same-size single-task students: 94.7-155% of teacher (Rusu, KL loss); 4x-smaller students: 108%; 15x-smaller: ~100%; 25x-smaller: 84% geometric mean. Multi-task consolidation: 10 games into one net (4x larger than one teacher) = 89.3% of the 10 specialists; 3 games into a SAME-size net = 116.9% (beating jointly-trained multi-task DQN's 83.5%). Actor-Mimic: near-expert 7/8 games, same-size net. Kickstarted students routinely EXCEED teachers (+42-43%) because the RL term stays on.
findings.source: Rusu et al. arXiv:1511.06295 Tables 1, 2, B1, B2, Fig 3-4 (read from PDF); Parisotto et al. arXiv:1511.06342 Fig 1/Table 1; Schmitt et al. arXiv:1803.03835 Sec 5
findings.relevance: Calibration for the fallback: a 128-hidden student consolidating 6 cells from 2 teachers should land at >=90% of each teacher's per-cell success rate under pure distillation, and can exceed teachers if RL stays in the loss. A cell at <<90% signals a routing/state-distribution bug, not capacity — consistent with your counter-evidence that 128 hidden already holds tight+loose in one net.

findings.claim: Entropy management with near-deterministic teachers: kickstarting deliberately keeps the A3C entropy bonus next to the distill term so the student explores beyond teacher supervision; Czarnecki notes the CE direction matters — H(teacher||student) replicates the teacher's full distribution, H(student||teacher) merely finds one teacher mode. Modern LLM practice (Thinking Machines, Oct 2025) independently converged on student-sampled trajectories + reverse KL against teacher log-probs for near-deterministic teachers, reporting RL-level gains at ~9-30x less compute.
findings.source: Schmitt et al. arXiv:1803.03835 Sec 2.2; Czarnecki et al. AISTATS 2019 Sec 3.3; thinkingmachines.ai/blog/on-policy-distillation (2025)
findings.relevance: Converged PPO teachers here are near-one-hot; distilling them will collapse student entropy unless a small entropy bonus is kept in the distill objective — otherwise the subsequent RL polish has no exploration left. Forward CE (teacher as target) + entropy bonus is the safe default for Discrete(31).

findings.claim: Consolidation-pattern warning: in SEQUENTIAL settings, distillation itself forgets — Progress & Compress needed online-EWC protection on the knowledge base during each compress/distill phase. All successful multi-teacher consolidations (Rusu 10-game, Actor-Mimic 8-game, kickstarting multi-teacher) distilled all teachers SIMULTANEOUSLY with interleaved per-task data, not one teacher after another.
findings.source: Schwarz et al., 'Progress & Compress', ICML 2018, PMLR v80; contrast with Rusu/Parisotto/Schmitt above; see also DisCoRL, arXiv:1907.05855
findings.relevance: The fallback must distill the generalist's 5 cells and the tight cell in one mixed stream from day one. Do not 'first clone the generalist, then add tight' — that recreates the seesaw inside supervised learning.

findings.claim: Concrete recipe spec synthesized from the above: (1) student = fresh Linear(38->128)+LSTM(128)+Discrete(31) net, same arch; (2) student collects rollouts across the 6-cell mixture with cell-balanced episode sampling; (3) per step, the cell's assigned teacher (generalist for its 5 cells, tight specialist for tight) is unrolled in lockstep on the student's obs, teacher probs stored in the rollout buffer; (4) loss = PPO loss (env reward incl. shaping, entropy bonus on) + lambda * CE(teacher_probs, student_probs) at tau=1, lambda_0 ~ 1.0 decayed exponentially to ~0 over the run (QDagger weaning), one lambda per teacher; (5) value head trains on returns throughout — no teacher V needed; (6) optional pure polish afterward keeps a small KL-to-distilled-checkpoint anchor. Expected: >=90% of each teacher per cell, plausibly >100% given the RL term.
findings.source: Synthesis of Schmitt et al. 1803.03835 (joint loss, multi-teacher, LSTM), Czarnecki et al. AISTATS 2019 (student-driven control), Rusu et al. 1511.06295 (loss/targets), Agarwal et al. 2206.01626 (lambda weaning), Vinyals et al. 2019 (polish anchor)
findings.relevance: Drop-in fallback plan for this repo: teacher checkpoints already exist (generalist + tight specialist from the 2-rung ladder); the only new plumbing is lockstep teacher inference during rollout collection and one extra CE term in the PPO update — no new training infrastructure.

design_risks: T13 defends the tight skill only via 25% reward-weight rehearsal, but the project's own replicated mechanism says in-mixture RL cannot REBUILD a skill once lost — so if tight erodes at any point in the 100M run there is no recovery path inside T13. A kickstarting-style auxiliary CE from the tight-specialist teacher applied only on tight-cell episodes (small fixed lambda, e.g. 0.1-0.5, optionally decayed) would convert tight's defense from reward-based to supervised and removes this single point of failure — it can be bolted onto T13 itself rather than reserved for the fallback.

If T13 seesaws and the fallback is implemented as offline BC on teacher-generated trajectories, the 3000-22000-step horizons put it in the maximal compounding-error regime (O(T^2*eps), Ross & Bagnell) and Czarnecki's 3x gap grows with horizon — the fallback is only sound student-driven, with teachers queried on student states online.

A two-phase fallback (pure supervised distill, then PPO polish with a fresh or stale critic) risks the documented fresh-critic collapse: noisy advantages destroy the cloned policy in early updates. Run distill jointly with PPO so the value head trains on returns throughout, or insert a critic-only warmup with frozen policy before polish.

Mixing the distill CE with env reward (which the joint recipe does, and T13's shaping guarantees) is exactly the regime where Czarnecki proves 1-step on-policy distillation can oscillate — mitigate by decaying lambda to zero (weaning) so late training is pure RL, and treat non-monotone per-cell curves during the mixed phase as expected rather than as failure.

Near-deterministic PPO teachers give near-one-hot targets: distilling them without an entropy bonus will collapse student entropy and strand the optional RL polish without exploration; conversely, do NOT apply Rusu's tau=0.01 sharpening — that result is for Q-value teachers, and sharpening an already-peaky softmax further destroys what little dark knowledge remains.

Cell-imbalanced gradient mass: sampling distillation minibatches proportional to env steps lets the 22000-step cells dominate the 3000-step tight cell by ~7x per episode — the same imbalance suspected in the seesaw. All successful multi-teacher consolidations used per-task buffers with balanced draws; the fallback (and arguably T13's mixture weights) should balance by episode/cell, not by steps.

Sequential distillation (clone generalist first, add tight after) recreates catastrophic forgetting inside supervised learning (Progress & Compress needed EWC for exactly this); the two teachers must be distilled simultaneously in one interleaved stream.
